On one occasion an individual said that Minister Stanisic had had trouble with them as well and that a decisive step could be expected from the ministry since we had been constantly reporting on problems with paramilitaries and paragroups, and a decisive action was to be expected from the ministry with a view to having these paramilitaries disarmed. This is what I heard from this one chap, and I expected orders to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you remember the driver's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember these lads. I know that, for a while, an individual by the name of Malovic was one of the escorts of Minister Stanisic. But later on, when I tried to cast my mind back to when it was exactly that he was there and when the regular special policemen were there, I simply could not set a time-frame on it. But it was one of those chaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, this paramilitary group that manhandled Minister Stanisic, you -- the record says that they were called the Angry Wasps. Were they the Angry Wasps or the Yellow Wasps; if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yellow, Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And according to the driver, where was Minister Stanisic mistreated by these Yellow Wasps? Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't the only one who suffered at their hand. This may have been the -- the drop, you know, the straw, the last straw. And, anyway, they would be stopping people, taking their goods and their monies. There was this earlier minister, I think Minister Ostojic, who was asked to lie on the ground and whatnot, and I suppose that this was then what tipped the scales and what made the ministry decide to engage in this confrontation with the paragroups and paramilitaries. I reported to Chief Cvijetic about these groups. On the one hand, we had the army established as an institution. On the other, we had the MUP established as an institution. They were the only force controlled by the local politicians who sponsored them. Now it was through the ministry, I don't know through which channels, that the decision was taken to engage in a showdown with these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. We're getting off-track. My question is: What municipality were these Yellow Wasps operating in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And when you had this conversation with Minister Stanisic's driver, where was Minister Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in passing. Normally, there would be one extra vehicle carrying his escort. But he was in passing because he was there on some other business. They would normally stop by only to have -- to take fuel and so on, and we spoke -- it was an informal conversation because he had heard of some developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And this incident with the Yellow Wasps and Minister Stanisic, when did that occur in relation to this conversation? Was it just the day before or -- when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident could have happened on that same day in the morning or the day before. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what was the incident? Can we just have that clarified briefly. Briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, can you -- once again, for the Trial Chamber's sake, could you clarify what the driver told you had happened to Minister Stanisic at the hands of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, they mistreated citizens, took their property from them, and the minister I spoke of was literally manhandled. They -- according to what I was told, they were telling him, So you, the minister, we're not going to let you go through. Go back to where you came from. And so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, in fact, after this conversation you had, was an operation conducted against the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was on that same day or a day or two later, that an order was issued that decisive action would be organised with a view to fighting the Wasps with the engagement of the special forces of the MUP with the participation of the Zvornik police station forces and some of the forces of the Vlasenica station, some 30 policemen I could spare and who were able to face up to the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: All right. Last topic. Were you aware of the destruction of any mosques in Vlasenica in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that this would happen some two or three hours earlier, since it was done by the engineering forces of the army. We were given advance notice of some two to three-hour, in order to make sure that the population living in the surrounding area was evacuated. As soon as we received notice of it, I instructed the policemen to go and inform the population in the surrounding area to leave the general area since we didn't know when the explosion would ensue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And do you remember, was this the VRS army of engineers, or was this the JNA, at this stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska. And the JNA was no longer there officially by August.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And how did the Muslim population react to this situation where the VRS was planning and organising the destruction of a mosque in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they couldn't know what was in offing, probably. But I suppose they were embittered. But there was only a handful of people there of Bosniak ethnicity by that time. But they must have been bitter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And could you tell us at approximately what time the mosque was actually destroyed that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that it was summertime, it was perhaps 8.00 or 9.00 in the evening, at dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did you inform the CSB about this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The information was released of this event. It had disturbed some of our -- or, rather, it is produced some work for us, since we received notice from citizens of their window-panes having been smashed and houses damaged, as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I just have a few minutes left. I'd actually show him one more question and at -- one more document and ask him two questions, essentially. Can we look at P866.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, we showed you this document during your interview last year and perhaps you had a look at it again during your proofing. It's a report from SJB Milici, Chief Bjelanovic, to CSB Romanija-Birac regarding killings near Nova Kasaba and is dated 3 August 1992. Were you aware of this incident concerning the killing of around 25 Muslims in Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave it some thought after reading the document, I made some connections and recalled that early on - I don't remember the date now - the TV reported on an incident in Kasaba, so everything I learned about it was from the TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What it -- was that in the -- what TV station? Was that international media or Serbian media or BiH media; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that by that time Serbian TV was in existence, but the footage was broadcast by the BBC or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And how many days after the incident itself was this broadcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day, perhaps, or a day or two later. At any rate, in the days that followed. Since that was the speed at which information was transmitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Are you aware whether this incident was ever investigated and prosecuted in the 1992 or 1993 time-period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-179 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because this was already within the area covered by the Milici police station, and they would have been the ones to take action, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can I just have one follow-up question before we give the floor to the Defence. In relation to the action that you told us was taken against the Yellow Wasps after having intimidate Mr. Stanisic, you said that a few days later action was taken. They were disarmed, I believe, and disbanded. And my question is: Do you know if they were subsequently prosecuted also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as I know, the individual, his -- he was called Zuco, I don't know his full name, and his brother also called Repic, he was convicted and imprisoned; I know that much. And if I may add, by your leave, the action was carried out efficiently in Zvornik. Similar problems existed in Bratunac and later on in Foca. This was a point in time when these paragroups and paramilitaries and local warmongers, if you will, were given a clear message that lawful institutions would take charge, and this was a period which I regard as one where institutions were being fully formed in order to make life easier. In that context, the Ministry of the Interior took decisive steps. It was difficult to take such a decision but we prevailed, and this was a turnaround in terms of institutions and their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: When did the -- when was the turnaround completed? So -- can you give us an approximate time of -- of when all these paramilitary groups were put to order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was process but this was the start. The strike there in Zvornik and then the next municipality was Bratunac. I couldn't follow closely the events further on. The unit was formed. The special unit of the police brigades of Republika Srpska, and then the next municipality was Foca. Wherever paramilitaries were present, interventions were made in order to normalise the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And so how were they normalised? Was the results of this attempt to discipline the volunteers and the paramilitary groups, was the result of that process that these groups were brought under the control of the VRS or were they simply disbanded and disappeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, some of these groups were driven away because they came from Serbia or wherever, and another part of members of these groups who remained in the area of Republika Srpska were mobilised into the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I believe the witness on page 56, line 2, said something about the municipality of Foca being next where the action was conducted and it was not recorded in the transcript. Thank you.
